content: Order lookups have been failing intermittently for weeks and support/ticket_3180.txt has the latest one. The relevant evidence is in lookup_failures.log, which pairs what the customer supplied with what the lookup actually received. Work out why these lookups miss when the order plainly exists, and recommend what the id emission rule should be so the same string always resolves no matter which system produced it or where the customer copied it from.

content:
## Analysis

The evidence in `lookup_failures.log` tells a clear story. Every portal miss is a **case-mismatch**:

| Portal lookup (input) | Result | Admin lookup | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ord-22f1` | miss | `ORD-22F1` | hit |
| `ord-22kb` | miss | `ORD-22KB` | hit |
| `ORD-22M4` | **hit** | — | — |
| `ord-22r9` | miss | `ORD-22R9` | hit |
| `Ord-22T7` | miss | `ORD-22T7` | hit |
| `ord-22v2` | miss | `ORD-22V2` | hit |

The one success (`ORD-22M4`) is the exception that proves the rule — the customer typed it in **uppercase** by chance.

The log's own annotation (lines 13–15) confirms the root cause:

> **fulfilment/printer emits:** `ORD-22V2` (uppercase)  
> **portal/self-service normalises to:** `ord-22v2` (lowercase)  
> **storage layer matches on the byte string as supplied** (case-sensitive)

The portal is **lowercasing** user input before querying a **case-sensitive** storage layer. The admin console doesn't do this, so it always hits. The customer in ticket 3180 pasted a packing-slip ID (uppercase) into chat, and the (admin-side) agent found it fine — but the self-service portal had lowercased it and got a miss.

---

## Recommended id emission rule

> **All order IDs must be emitted, stored, and queried in uppercase. Every system that accepts order ID input MUST normalize it to uppercase before sending it to the storage layer.**

This is a single, consistent rule that works everywhere:

| System | What to do |
|---|---|
| Printer / fulfilment | Emit `ORD-xxxx` (already uppercase — keep it) |
| Portal / self-service | `.toUpperCase()` on user input before querying |
| Admin console | Already uppercase — no change needed |
| Storage layer | Keep case-sensitive matching — but every caller sends uppercase |

No lowercasing. No mixed case. One canonical form: **uppercase**. This way it doesn't matter where the customer copied the ID from (packing slip, email, chat, or an agent reading it aloud) — the portal will uppercase it and the storage layer will find the match.

Yes, that is the cause. Decision: order ids are emitted lowercase, everywhere, by every service that issues or prints one, and every lookup lowercases its input before matching so a customer copying an id off a slip resolves the same record as one pasted out of the admin console. Anything that renders an id for a human renders it lowercase too, so what people see and what the system stores are the same string.
